source.title: UBVRI twilight sky brightness at ESO-Paranal
source.exactEvidence: Table 1 PDF page 4 (1-based); Table 2 PDF page 6 (1-based), independently visually checked against original PDF

observer.spatialSelection: Table 1 fitted sky frames have zenith distance <=40 deg, meaning sky altitude >=50 deg; mixed direction, NOT a fixed 45 or 80 degree ray
observer.time: archival FORS1 measurements; fits aggregate observations from multiple nights
observer.moon: long-exposure standard observations selected with Moon below horizon
observer.note: Table 1 empirical polynomial is based on real measurements, not a simulation, and is not a per-frame calibrated dataset

publishedFit.rmsMeaning: RMS scatter of measurements about the empirical fit; not instrument-only uncertainty or new-site prediction coverage

computedWithinBandV.interpret: total observed sky V reference at Paranal, not isolated solar-only flux

spectralDataLimit: Table 2 supplies genuine dated and direction-specific sky spectra within nominal V1 ray altitude. Figure 9 spectra were V-scaled and vertically shifted for display; raw spectral flux files and per-night measured atmosphere have NOT been retrieved, so no absolute spectral radiance was digitized or claimed
scientificLimitations: Published fits used mixed sky altitudes 50-90, including late-V1 OOD altitude>80; a matched <=80 raw-frame subset or rigorous angular envelope is required for validation
The empirical fit is only valid for solar depressions 5..15. Do not extrapolate its polynomial into 15..16 or beyond
Measured total V sky includes nightglow and other components; compare to explicit bandpass-convolved TOTAL sky with same atmosphere, not to raw solar-only MYSTIC spectra
No independent visual star first-visibility timestamp or controlled observer criterion is supplied by the paper
No exact coincident AOD vertical profile, local light pollution or site weather profile is included in this aggregate fixture
The study describes an observed transition to night-sky emission around sun depression 15..16; this is NOT evidence for physical zero solar radiance or no-new-stars behavior
nextFrozenBenchmarkRequirements: Select future raw frames independent of model residuals before computing any predictions
Match exact UTC, location, pointing alt/az, instrument response, moon/cloud status, aerosol extinction PROFILE and observer height
Pin one unchanged model SHA and atmosphere-state identity BEFORE reading comparison residuals
Report bandpass-matched total-sky log residual, per-night dispersion and angular/systematic sensitivity
No fit, tuning, release or universal first-star-time validation on this aggregate reference alone
